facts: The guide overview organises the HM Land Registry plans guidance into six supplements.
Supplement 2 is designed to assist preparation of deed plans.
Supplement 3 covers general boundaries, boundary ownership and maintenance.
Practice guide 40 supplement 5 was updated on 13 July 2026.
A registered title consists of the title plan, the register and filed documents referred to in the register.
A title plan graphically represents the general extent and normally shows general boundaries.
Practice guide 40 supplement 4 was updated on 1 June 2026.
The guide explains boundary agreements and determined boundaries.
A determined boundary is recorded in affected registers and a filed plan identifies the exact line.
Form DB applies to England and Wales.
Form DB is used to apply for an exact boundary line to be shown as a determined boundary.
The guidance describes a determined boundary as the line agreed between neighbouring parties.
The live scheduled-monument dataset reports 20,150 records.
The scheduled-monument list is kept and maintained by Historic England.
The page reports one provider, collector run 27 July 2026 and new data found 25 July 2026.
The live listed-building-outline dataset reports 124,897 records.
The outlines are incomplete, do not consistently show curtilage and are an indicative guide only.
The live battlefield dataset reports 94 records.
The data represents Historic England designated battlefields and reports authoritative-source origin.
The live Article 4 direction area dataset reports 7,152 records.
Article 4 areas can require planning applications for works otherwise classed as permitted development.
The live green-belt dataset reports 190 records.
Annual March returns are published in autumn and form a snapshot that may not reflect later boundary changes.
The dataset reports one provider and authoritative-source origin.
Zone 1 is least likely and zone 3 more likely to flood, but zones do not prove whether or how severely a place will flood.
The live protected-wreck-site dataset reports 58 records.
The dataset reports one provider and authoritative-source origin.
Protected wrecks may be designated under the 1973, 1979 and 1986 Acts and can be designated heritage assets for planning.
The local-green-space dataset currently reports zero records.
The dataset currently reports zero providers.
The page reports no collector attempt and no date for newly found data.
Environment Agency site-specific LIDAR surveys in the time-stamped DTM archive date from 1998.
Available resolutions include 25 centimetres, 50 centimetres, 1 metre and 2 metres.
The data is supplied as 5 kilometre GeoTIFF ZIP files aligned to the OS Grid, referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn and states plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
The 2 metre composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DTM uses last or only returns and removes surface objects to represent terrain.
The 2022 composite combines time-stamped and National LIDAR Programme surveys, preferring newest best-resolution data and using bilinear interpolation when resampled.
The 1 metre composite DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The DSM includes vehicles, buildings, vegetation and the terrain surface.
The 2022 composite is available as GeoTIFF rasters in 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Environment Agency guidance lists WCS 2.0.1 endpoints for composite DTM products and other elevation services.
WCS is described as an OGC standard for serving and retrieving multidimensional coverages.
WCS enables requests for raw pixel values such as elevation.
OS Terrain 50 supplies a 50 metre grid in ASCII and GML and 10 metre contours in shapefile, GML, GeoPackage and vector tiles.
The product is available as an online download with no registration required.
The tiled national supply contains 2,858 ten-kilometre tiles in 55 folders and is resupplied annually in July.
ASCII grid is a generic text DTM format readable by standard GIS software.
Each 10 kilometre tile has 200 rows and columns of 50 metre pixels.
Heights are calculated at pixel centres and supplied to the nearest 0.1 metre.
OS Terrain 50 contour layers are supplied in GML 3.2.1.
Spot heights are selected automatically as the highest mass point within closed contours and equal-height points are removed.
Spot-height z values are rounded to zero decimal places and genuine depressions may produce values below surrounding contours.
The OS Data Hub page reports Great Britain coverage and a July 2026 version date.
The page lists ASCII Grid and GML grid supply plus shapefile, GML, GeoPackage and vector-tile formats.
The product is free OpenData downloadable under the Open Government Licence.
